==English== [[File:Palomena prasina, Budapest, Hungary - 20101021.jpg|thumb|A [[w:green shield bug|green shield bug]] ({{taxlink|Palomena prasina|species}}) in [[w:Budapest|Budapest]], [[w:Hungary|Hungary]]. It is an [[insect]] of the [[order]] {{taxfmt|Hemiptera|order}}, and so is one of the "true bugs".]] ===Alternative forms=== * {{alter|en|bugg||obsolete}} ===Etymology=== First attested in this form around 1620 (referring to a “[[bedbug]]”), from earlier {{m|en|bugge||beetle}}, from {{der|en|enm|bugge||scarecrow, hobgoblin}} which is traced alternatively to: * a Celtic root found in {{cog|sco|bogill||goblin, bugbear}} and obsolete {{cog|cy|bwg||ghost, hobgoblin}}; compare Welsh {{m|cy|bwgwl||threat, fear}} and {{cog|mga|bocanách||supernatural being}}. * {{der|en|gem-pro|*bugja-||swollen up, thick}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*bʰew-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*bu-||to swell}};{{R:ine:IEW|98-102}} compare {{cog|no|bugge||big man}}, dialectal Low German {{m|nds|Bögge||goblin, snot}}. * or to a word related to {{m|en|buck}} and originally referring to a goat-shaped spectre.{{R:Online Etymology Dictionary|accessdate=12 June 2025}} For the “insect” meaning the assonance with {{der|en|enm|budde||beetle}}, from {{der|en|ang|budda}}, from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*buʀdō}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*buzdô}}, from the same ultimate source as above, might have played a role. Compare {{cog|nds|Budde|t=louse, grub}}, {{cog|no|budda|t=newborn domestic animal}}, {{cog|is|budda|t=purse}}. More at {{l|en|bud}}. But ultimately this convergence of meaning doesn't prove a conflation of the two terms; they might have existed in parallel since PIE times with similar meanings, even if unnoticed by literary sources. The term is used to refer to technical errors and problems at least as early as the 19th century, predating the commonly known story of a moth being caught in a computer. {{attn|en|ety of Morse telegraph key? see [[w:Vibroplex]]}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|bŭg}} * {{IPA|en|/bʌɡ/|a=RP,GA}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-bug.ogg|a=US}} * {{IPA|en|/bɐɡ/|a=AU,NZ}} * {{IPA|en|/bʊɡ/|a=Northern England}} * {{rhymes|en|ʌɡ|s=1}} * {{hyphenation|en|bug}} ===Noun=== {{en-noun}} # {{senseid|en|Q26371}} {{lb|en|entomology}} An [[insect]] of the order {{taxfmt|Hemiptera|order}} (the “[[true bug#English:_Q26371|true bug]]s”). #* {{quote-book|en|year=1869|author={{w|Alfred Russel Wallace}}|title={{w|The Malay Archipelago}}|publisher=Macmillan and Co.|year_published=|volume=II|location=London|page=199|passage=Several pretty beetles, a superb "'''bug'''," and a few nice land-shells were obtained, and I returned in the afternoon well satisfied with my first trial of the promised land.}} # {{lb|en|informal|proscribed}} Any [[motile]] small [[terrestrial]] [[invertebrate]], especially one that is seen as a [[pest]]. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1874|author=Henry Sampson|title=A history of advertising|page=278 |passage=Speaking of advertising changes of name, a title by which those lodging-house pests, '''bugs''', are now often known, that of [[Norfolk Howard]]s, is derived from an advertisement in which one Ephraim Bug avowed his intention of being for the future known as Norfolk Howard.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1910|author=Aristotle|title=The Works of Aristotle: Historia animalium|translator=D.W. Thompson |text='''Bugs''' are generated from the moisture of living animals, as it dries up outside their bodies. Lice are generated out of the flesh of animals.}} #: {{ux|en|These flies are a bother. I’ll get some '''bug''' spray and kill them.}} # {{senseid|en|Q6865172}} {{lb|en|informal}} Any [[minibeast]]. ## Any [[insect]], [[arachnid]], [[myriapod]] or [[entognath]]. ### {{senseid|en|Q1390}} Any [[insect]]. ###: {{ux|en|A: Eew, what is that thing?! Is that a '''bug'''?! B: No, it's a spider. And don't worry: she's not gonna hurt you.}} ### {{senseid|en|marine crustacean}} Any of various species of marine (saltwater or freshwater) [[crustacean]]s; e.g. a [[Moreton Bay bug]], [[mudbug]]. ###* {{quote-journal|en|date=Feb 2021|journal= The Road Ahead|location=Brisbane|page=39|column=2|text='''Bugs''', oysters, prawns and crabs {{...}} are plated up on the decks of four side-by-side trawlers bobbing on the calm waters of Trinity Inlet.}} ### {{lb|en|paleontology|slang}} A [[trilobite]]. ###* {{quote-book|en|year=2007|author=Kirk Johnson|title=Cruisin' the Fossil Freeway|page=174 |passage=We asked Harris if he had any recommendations about seeing the famous trilobite digs. He said we should just drive out to his claim in the Wheeler Quadrangle, and it was just fine with him if we dug a few '''bugs'''.}} ### {{lb|en|Maine}} A [[lobster]]. ### {{lb|en|UK|obsolete|specifically}} A [[bedbug]]. # {{senseid|en|Q179550}}{{lb|en|chiefly|_|computing|engineering|_|jargon}} A [[problem]] that needs [[fixing]]. #: {{syn|en|defect|glitch}} #: {{ux|en|The software '''bug''' led the computer to calculate 2 plus 2 as 3.}} # A contagious [[illness]], or a [[pathogen]] causing it. #: {{ux|en|He's got the flu '''bug'''.}} # {{lb|en|informal}} An [[enthusiasm]] for something; an [[obsession]]. #: {{ux|en|I caught the skiing '''bug''' while staying in the Alps.}} #* {{RQ:Kerouac On the Road|part=1|chapter=1|passage=As we rode in the bus in the weird phosphorescent void of the Lincoln Tunnel we leaned on each other with fingers waving and yelled and talked excitedly, and I was beginning to get the '''bug''' like Dean.}} #* {{quote-song|en|lyricist={{w|Bobby Darin}} and {{w|Murray Kaufman}}|title={{w|Splish Splash (song)|Splish Splash}}|artist={{w|Bobby Darrin}}||year=1958|text=Bing bang, I saw the whole gang
Dancing on my living room rug, yeah
Flip flop they was doing the bop
All the teens had the dancing '''bug'''.}} # {{lb|en|informal}} A keen [[enthusiast]] or [[hobbyist]]. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1961|author=Fredric Brown|title=Nightmare in Yellow |passage=His mother had been a '''bug''' on astrology, which was why the moment of his birth had been impressed on him so exactly.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|year=1961|journal=Kiplinger's Personal Finance|volume=15|issue=12|page=34 |passage=Incidentally, the camera manufacturers have had a new worry—that they might "kill off the hobby," as U.S. Camera magazine put it recently—by automating to the point that real camera '''bugs''' would feel no challenge.}} # A [[concealed]] [[electronic]] [[eavesdropping]] or [[intercept]] [[device]] #: {{syn|en|wire}} #: {{ux|en|We installed a '''bug''' in her telephone.}} # A small and usually [[invisible]] [[file]] (traditionally a single-[[pixel]] [[image]]) on a [[World Wide Web]] page, primarily used to [[track]] [[user]]s. #: {{ux|en|He suspected the image was a Web '''bug''' used for determining who was visiting the site.}} # {{lb|en|television}} A small, usually [[transparent]] or [[translucent]] [[image]] placed in a corner of a [[television]] program to identify the broadcasting [[network]] or [[cable]] [[channel]]. #: {{ux|en|Channel 4's '''bug''' distracted Jim from his favorite show.}} #: {{ux|en|The score '''bug''' displays the current football score over the ongoing match.}} # {{lb|en|aviation}} A [[manually]] [[position]]ed [[marker]] in [[flight instrument]]s. #* {{quote-journal|en|year=2004|journal=Flying Magazine|volume=131|issue=10|page=10 |passage=You look up the proper speed for the phase of flight, set the reminder '''bug''', and then literally forget the speed. You don't read the airspeed number, you fly to the '''bug'''.}} # A semi-automated [[telegraph key]]. # {{lb|en|obsolete}} [[hobgoblin|Hobgoblin]], [[scarecrow]]; anything that terrifies. {{defdate|late 14th c.–early 17th. c}} #: {{syn|en|bog|bogey|bogle|boggle|boggard|bugbear}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Winter's Tale|act=III|scene=ii|passage=Sir, spare your threats: / The '''bug''' which you would fright me with I seek.}} # {{lb|en|chiefly|LGBTQ|often preceded by ''the''}} [[HIV]]. #* {{quote-book |en |year=2019 |author=Tora Holmberg; Annika Jonsson; Fredrik Palm |title=Death Matters: Cultural Sociology of Mortal Life |publisher=Springer |isbn=9783030114855 |page=130 |passage=The arguably most debated bareback practice that came to attract attention early on (and still does) was that of "'''bug''' chasing," in which HIV-negative men ('''bug''' chasers) actively seek out sex with HIV-positive men (gift givers).}} # {{lb|en|poker}} A limited form of [[wild card]] in some variants of [[poker]]. # {{lb|en|US|petroleum industry|slang|dated}} {{synonym of|en|oil bug}}. # {{lb|en|slang|US|horse-racing}} An [[asterisk]] denoting an [[apprentice]] [[jockey]]'s weight allowance. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1999|author=Anita Scialli|title=Inside Track 1999|page=62 |passage=The "'''bugs'''" are the asterisks next to the apprentice's name. One '''bug''' is a five-pound allowance, two '''bugs''' equal seven pounds, and three '''bugs''' equal ten pounds.}} # {{lb|en|slang|US|horse-racing|by extension}} A [[young]] [[apprentice]] [[jockey]]. #: {{syn|en|bug boy}} # {{lb|en|printing}} {{synonym of|en|union bug}}. # {{lb|en|gambling|slang}} A small piece of [[metal]] used in a [[slot machine]] to block certain winning combinations. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1961|author=John Scarne|title=Complete Guide to Gambling|page=394 |passage=Because many illegal slot-machine operators here and abroad do not like to give the slot-machine player even one chance to hit the jackpot or the big bonus, they make use of a "'''bug'''." This is a small, flat half-circle of iron about an inch long, which looks something like a bug.}} # {{lb|en|gambling|slang}} A metal clip attached to the underside of a table, etc. to hold hidden cards, as a form of cheating. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1897|author=Robert Frederick Foster|title=Foster's Complete Hoyle|page=195 |passage=Some clumsy or audacious sharpers will go so far as to hold out cards in their lap, or stick them in a "'''bug'''" under the table.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2006|author=Jon Sharpe|title=The Trailsman #299: Dakota Danger |passage=Fargo had been in a saloon in Kansas when a man was caught using a '''bug'''. Made of steel and shaped like a money clip with two sharp ends, the '''bug''' was jammed under a table and held cards the bug's owner palmed until they were needed.}} ====Synonyms==== * See also
